title: AI Superpowers
subtitle: China, Silicon Valley, and the New World Order
pitch: A veteran of Apple, Microsoft and Google China argues that AI is now about execution and data, which favours China, and that the real crisis will be jobs.

chapters.g: AlphaGo's 2016 and 2017 wins over top Go players woke China up to AI.
How brutal competition among Chinese startups built tough entrepreneurs.
Mobile payments and super apps give Chinese firms rich real world data.
Comparing the US and China on research, data, talent and government support.
Internet AI, business AI, perception AI and autonomous AI.

chapters.t: Utopia, dystopia, and the real AI crisis
chapters.g: Lee sets aside superintelligence fears and focuses on job losses and inequality.
His cancer diagnosis changed how he thinks about work and love.

chapters.t: A blueprint for human co-existence with AI
chapters.g: A future where people do caring and creative work machines cannot.
How countries might share the gains and handle the disruption together.

ideas: We moved from the age of discovery to the age of implementation.
Data and execution matter more than breakthroughs.
AI will hit jobs and widen inequality.
Human care and love are where people will stay valuable.

args.a: China has the edge in deploying AI.
args.c: The later large language model race was led by US labs, with chips and compute proving decisive.

args.a: Superintelligence worries are a distraction from jobs.
args.c: Many researchers, including some who signed later warnings, think both are real and that the risks are not either or.

questions: What jobs in your area need human care most?
Is AI a race between countries or a shared project?
Does Lee's view still hold after ChatGPT?

quiz.q: What event does Lee call China's Sputnik moment?
quiz.w: Go is hugely popular in China.

quiz.q: How many waves of AI does he describe?
What does Lee see as the real crisis?
